title: This World of Tomorrow by Tom Hanks and James Glossman at The Shed #t...
transcript: For a play called This World of Tomorrow, it sure harps on the past. Currently running at The Shed and starring Tom Hanks, who is also a co-writer on the project, This World of Tomorrow follows a man named Bert in 2089 and 1939. He initially goes back in time to do some vaguely described historical research for work and has a chance encounter at the New York World's Fair with a woman named Carmen, played by the always lovely Kelli O'Hara. This changes the course of Bert's research, and he repeatedly goes back to that day to relive it as much as he can. From a science fiction standpoint, we don't get too much context for the actual time traveling, nor do we get much context into who Bert really is and the life he's led up to this point in 2089. The fact that we get more background on Carmen in 1939 than any other character, which we can attribute to Bert's curiosities about her, indicates that the old timeline is the emotional core of the piece. It represents wonder and curiosity, and an optimism that has arguably fizzled out in the modern day. Other than some minor plot holes that I'm more or less willing to overlook, the play is cute, albeit a little saccharine for my taste. It's definitely for folks in a similar age bracket to Tom Hanks who may find it charmingly nostalgic, but to me, it was not that interesting. I will say though, Tom Hanks and Kelli O'Hara do a great job exuding that charm and nostalgia, and they have wonderful chemistry together. While I wouldn't call this riveting theatre, I enjoyed it for what it is, and I can see the target audience getting a decent kick out of it. With that, another program for my collection.
